Task: Streaming Speech-to-Text

Write code that streams audio chunks from an async source using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Deepgram:
  Service: Deepgram Streaming API
  SDK: deepgram-sdk
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: listen.websocket, transcribe
  Setup hints: DEEPGRAM_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/lower-level-websockets

Option 2 — Amazon Transcribe Streaming:
  Service: Amazon Transcribe Streaming
  SDK: amazon-transcribe / boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_stream_transcription
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/streaming.html

Option 3 — DashScope Real-time ASR:
  Service: DashScope real-time speech recognition
  SDK: dashscope
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: RecognitionCallback, streaming call
  Setup hints: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/real-time-speech-recognition

Option 4 — Azure Speech Streaming:
  Service: Azure AI Speech streaming
  SDK: azure-cognitiveservices-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_continuous_recognition, recognized
  Setup hints: AZURE_SPEECH_KEY, AZURE_SPEECH_REGION
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/how-to-recognize-speech

Option 5 — Watson STT WebSocket:
  Service: Watson Speech to Text WebSocket
  SDK: ibm-watson
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: recognize_using_websocket
  Setup hints: IBM_STT_APIKEY, IBM_STT_URL
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/speech-to-text?topic=speech-to-text-websockets

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import asyncio
import os
from dotenv import load_dotenv

# Load environment variables from .env file
load_dotenv()

# Deepgram setup
from deepgram import (
    DeepgramClient,
    DeepgramClientOptions,
    LiveTranscriptionEvents,
    LiveOptions,
)

async def stream_audio_to_text(audio_stream_source):
    """
    Streams audio chunks from an async source to Deepgram for speech-to-text transcription.

    Args:
        audio_stream_source: An async generator that yields audio chunks (bytes).
    """
    DEEPGRAM_API_KEY = os.getenv("DEEPGRAM_API_KEY")
    if not DEEPGRAM_API_KEY:
        raise ValueError("DEEPGRAM_API_KEY environment variable not set.")

    config: DeepgramClientOptions = DeepgramClientOptions(
        verbose=1 # Adjust verbosity as needed
    )
    client = DeepgramClient(DEEPGRAM_API_KEY, config)

    # Example of setting up a connection to Deepgram's live transcription API
    # You might want to adjust model, language, and other options based on your needs
    live_connection = client.listen.asynclive.v("1")

    async def on_message(self, result, **kwargs):
        sentence = result.channel.alternatives[0].transcript
        if sentence:
            print(f"Deepgram received: {sentence}")

    async def on_error(self, error, **kwargs):
        print(f"Deepgram error: {error}")

    live_connection.on(LiveTranscriptionEvents.Transcript, on_message)
    live_connection.on(LiveTranscriptionEvents.Error, on_error)

    print("Connecting to Deepgram...")
    await live_connection.start(LiveOptions(model="nova-2", language="en-US", interim_results=True))
    print("Deepgram connection started.")

    try:
        async for chunk in audio_stream_source():
            if live_connection.get_state() == 1: # Check if connection is open
                await live_connection.send(chunk)
            else:
                print("Deepgram connection not open, stopping audio stream.")
                break
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error sending audio: {e}")
    finally:
        print("Finishing Deepgram connection...")
        await live_connection.finish()
        print("Deepgram connection finished.")

# Example async generator for simulating an audio stream
async def simulate_audio_stream():
    # In a real application, this would read from a microphone, a file, etc.
    # For demonstration, we'll yield empty bytes periodically.
    # Replace with actual audio data for meaningful transcription.
    audio_chunk_size = 1024 # Example chunk size
    num_chunks = 5

    for i in range(num_chunks):
        print(f"Yielding simulated audio chunk {i+1}/{num_chunks}...")
        # Simulate an audio chunk (e.g., raw audio bytes)
        # For actual transcription, this must be valid audio data.
        yield b"\x00" * audio_chunk_size
        await asyncio.sleep(1) # Simulate delay between chunks
    print("Simulated audio stream finished.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # To run this example, ensure you have a DEEPGRAM_API_KEY set in your .env file
    # and deepgram-sdk installed (`pip install deepgram-sdk python-dotenv`).
    # This example will connect to Deepgram and send silent audio, so you won't get
    # meaningful transcripts unless you replace `b"\x00" * audio_chunk_size`
    # with actual audio data.
    asyncio.run(stream_audio_to_text(simulate_audio_stream))
